body:
Welcome to SPLogbook — an advanced, modern amateur radio logging and station automation environment built in Rust.

1. Initial Setup: Open Settings → Station & Operator Setup to enter your station callsign (e.g. SP6INA), operator name, Maidenhead grid locator (e.g. JO81), and optional CQ/ITU zones.

2. Connecting Your Radio (CAT): Open Radio → CAT / Hamlib Radio Connection and choose the backend matching your transceiver (Hamlib rigctld, FLRig, TCI, Icom CI-V, Kenwood, Yaesu, Elecraft, or FlexRadio SmartSDR). Once connected, VFO frequency, mode, and signal reports synchronize in real time.

3. Connecting to a DX Cluster: Open the DX Cluster tab or floating window, select a server preset (e.g. dxcluster.pl:8000, dxfun.com:8000, w3lpl.net:7373), and click 'Connect'. Clicking any DX spot automatically tunes your radio and populates the QSO entry form.

4. Logging a QSO: Enter the correspondent's callsign in the Callsign field and press Enter or F2. SPLogbook immediately resolves the DXCC prefix, calculates bearing and distance, queries online Callbooks (QRZ/HamQTH), and checks award status (ATNO / New Band / New Mode).

Tip: Press Ctrl+Shift+P at any time to open the Command Palette and invoke any application feature from the keyboard.
title: 1. Getting Started

body:
SPLogbook provides the modern NATIVE-CAT async rig control architecture powered by the RigHub multi-radio core and the TxArbiter interlock. It supports 8 dedicated hardware and network backends:

- Hamlib (rigctld): Standard TCP network backend (default port 4532) or background supervisor launching bundled/system rigctld on your serial port.
- Icom CI-V: Direct native binary communication (CI-V $FE $FE ... $FD frames) via serial COM or TCP with auto-address discovery (e.g. 0x94 for IC-7300, 0xA2 for IC-705) and collision backoff.
- Kenwood: Direct native asynchronous ASCII serial CAT (FA, FB, MD, TX, RX, IF commands) with a streaming buffered parser.
- Yaesu: Multi-generational support including CAT-V (5-byte binary frames for FT-817/857/897), ASCII (FT-dx10, FT-991A, FT-710), and CAT-III/IV/IX generations.
- Elecraft: Native support for K2, K3, K3S, KX2, KX3, and K4 transceivers (with serial COM or direct K4 TCP network transport).
- FlexRadio: Native SmartSDR TCP API integration (v2.0–3.x) with slice/meter subscriptions and automatic LAN discovery via UDP broadcast (port 4992).
- FLRig (XML-RPC): Seamless integration with the popular FLRig transceiver control server.
- TCI (Transceiver Control Interface): High-speed WebSocket integration with SDR transceivers (Expert Electronics SunSDR2 PRO/DX, Thetis, ExpertSDR3).

Multi-Radio Core & RF Safety:
- RigHub & TxArbiter: Full dual-rig configuration support (Radio 1 & Radio 2) with a strict transmit arbiter (TxArbiter) enforcing a Single-TX Interlock and zero retry on SetPtt(true) to protect power amplifiers.
- Safe Read-Only Probe: Port detection and handshake probing is strictly non-invasive (read-only), with zero register mutations and zero TX emission.
- Antenna Rotator Control: Built-in rotctld client (TCP port 4533) rotates your antenna with a single click to the Short Path or Long Path azimuth from spots, map, or log.
- CAT Port Sharing: Built-in Hamlib proxy server (port 4534) allows external digital programs (WSJT-X, JTDX, FLDigi) to share the same radio simultaneously without port conflicts.
- HIL Test Harness: Laboratory Hardware-in-the-Loop harness requiring mandatory 50 Ω dummy load termination and strictly prohibiting PTT tests on live antennas.
title: 2. Station & CAT Setup

body:
At the core of SPLogbook is an SQLite database running in WAL (Write-Ahead Logging) mode:

- Data safety: WAL mode with transactional writes protects the log against corruption, even after a sudden power loss.
- Fast search: dedicated indexes keep searching and filtering instant, even in logs with hundreds of thousands of QSOs.
- Smart QSO entry form: callsigns are converted to upper case, Super Check Partial (SCP) suggests calls, likely typos are offered as corrections and the prefix is matched against the country files.
- Duplicate detection: a [DUPE!] warning appears as soon as a station has already been worked on the current band and mode.
- QSO audio recorder: record receiver audio from the sound card and attach the WAV file to the QSO.
- Multiple journals: keep separate logs (home station, club callsign, /P activations, contests).

Backups (Settings → Backups):
- A periodic copy every 30 minutes by default. It is made in the background and only when the database has changed since the previous copy; 0 turns periodic copies off.
- A copy when the program closes and, if enabled, an ADIF copy of the active log next to it.
- The last 10 copies are kept by default (Number of backups to keep).
- Copies are saved in the backups folder next to the database file. Log → Database Backup makes a copy at any time.
- If the previous session did not close normally, the program checks the database at the next start and saves a separate copy marked unclean_shutdown (the last 5 are kept).
- Copies made before a database upgrade (pre_migration) are never deleted automatically.
title: 3. QSO Logging & SQLite DB

body:
SPLogbook is designed for fast, hands-on-keyboard operation without reaching for the mouse:

Function Keys (Primary):
- F1 — Help window and complete keyboard shortcuts reference
- F2 — Save current QSO (Contest & DX standard)
- F3 — Wipe QSO entry form and focus Callsign input
- F4 — Force immediate online Callbook lookup (QRZ / HamQTH)
- F5 — Refresh logbook table from database
- F6 — Open Send DX Spot dialog
- F7 — No action on its own; transmit is explicit: Ctrl+Shift+F7 requests TX ON and Ctrl+F7 requests TX OFF via CAT (blocked while editing text, during IME composition, when a modal window is open or when the window is unfocused; TX ON also requires authorization)
- F8 — Open Voice Keyer panel
- F11 — Toggle Fullscreen mode
- F12 — Open built-in User Manual (this window)

Modifier Shortcuts (Ctrl / Cmd):
- Ctrl+N — New QSO (clears form and focuses Callsign)
- Ctrl+W — Wipe QSO form
- Ctrl+S — Save station configuration and database
- Ctrl+F — Open Advanced Logbook Filter
- Ctrl+L — Focus / toggle Logbook table
- Ctrl+D — Open / toggle DX Cluster panel
- Ctrl+B — Open Bandmap window
- Ctrl+M — Open World Map & Grayline Terminator
- Ctrl+K — Open CW Keyer & Macros terminal
- Ctrl+P — Open Station Profiles manager
- Ctrl+E — Open configurable CSV Exporter
- Ctrl+I — Open ADIF Import dialog
- Ctrl+T — Cycle UI color theme (Dark / Daylight / High-Contrast)
- Ctrl+Z — Undo last deleted QSO
- Ctrl+Y / Ctrl+Shift+Z — Redo
- Ctrl+Shift+S — Open Statistics & Charts window
- Ctrl+Shift+P — Open Command Palette
- Ctrl+Q — Safely exit application
title: 4. Keyboard Shortcuts

body:
The DX Cluster module delivers real-time DX spots and award alerts:

- Built-in Telnet Client: Connects to any DXSpider, AR-Cluster, or CC-Cluster node with automatic reconnection and live command input (e.g. sh/dx 25).
- Smart Deduplication: Sliding window filter prevents duplicate spots from flooding your table.
- Visual & Audio Alerts:
* Magenta Star (ATNO): All-Time New One DXCC entity with optional audio chime.
* Emerald Badge: New Band or New Mode for a worked DXCC country.
- Advanced Filtering: Filter by HF / WARC / VHF bands, modes (CW, SSB, FT8/FT4, Digi), continent, or hide automated RBN skimmer spots.
- Click-to-Tune: Clicking any spot tunes your transceiver VFO to the spot frequency, sets the mode, and populates the QSO entry form.
- Visual Bandmap: Real-time frequency scale displaying active stations with age-based color fading.
title: 5. DX Cluster & Bandmap

body:
SPLogbook combines an ionospheric model with current space-weather data:

- Space weather (HamQTH): Solar Flux Index (SFI), sunspot number (SSN), geomagnetic A and K indices, X-ray flux, geomagnetic field state and the latitude of the auroral oval. Click Refresh in the Solar Weather & Propagation panel to download them.
- VOACAP-lite HF engine: computes the great-circle midpoint, the solar zenith angle, D-layer absorption, foF2, MUF, LUF and FOT, the band opening probability (0-100%) and the expected S-meter reading.
- Band forecast: calculated from your station locator to the correspondent's locator when it is in the QSO form, otherwise towards the continents. Without solar data or without your station locator no forecast is shown.
- Propagation badge: when the correspondent's locator is known, the QSO form shows the predicted reliability on the current band.
- Explanation: the Operator Assistant window lists why a band is open or closed (solar activity, geomagnetic storm, day or night on the path, D-layer absorption).
- EME planner: real-time Moon azimuth, elevation, range, Doppler shift, path loss, degradation and mutual visibility windows.
title: 6. HF Propagation, Solar & EME

body:
SPLogbook integrates directly with external digital mode suites:

- WSJT-X / JTDX UDP Bridge (port 2237):
* Decodes binary UDP frames: Heartbeat, Status, Decode, QSO Logged, and Clear.
* Automatically logs completed FT8/FT4/JT65/Q65 QSOs with exact SNR dB reports and grid locators.
* Highlights calling stations in real time when they represent an ATNO or new band/mode.
- JS8Call (JSON TCP/UDP port 2442): Captures RX.ACTIVITY, RIG.FREQ, and LOG.QSO frames.
- FLDigi (XML-RPC port 7362): Reads frequency, mode, and QSO fields for PSK31, RTTY, Olivia, and Contestia.
- N1MM UDP Broadcasts: Emits standard XML ContactInfo packets so tools like GridTracker track your logged QSOs.
title: 7. Digital Modes (WSJT-X, JS8, FLDigi)

body:
Dedicated tools for LEO amateur satellites and the QO-100 geostationary transponder:

- SGP4/SDP4 Orbital Propagator: Uses NORAD Two-Line Elements (TLE) with one-click online updates.
- Live Orbital Telemetry: Computes azimuth, elevation, slant range, radial velocity, and ground footprint.
- Automatic CAT Doppler Correction: Continuously calculates uplink and downlink Doppler shift:
Δf = -f0 * (v_slant / c)
and updates transceiver VFO frequencies via CAT.
- Azimuth/Elevation Rotator Tracking: Drives 2-axis satellite rotators via rotctld.
title: 8. Satellite Tracking & Doppler

body:
Real-time audio spectrum analyzer and waterfall display:

- Cross-Platform Audio Capture (cpal): Captures audio directly from your transceiver USB audio codec, line-in, or virtual audio cable.
- RustFFT Engine: Fast Hann-windowed FFT computation minimizing spectral leakage.
- Configurable Controls:
* FFT sizes: 512, 1024, 2048, or 4096 bins.
* Adjustable Gain (dB), Noise Floor (dB), and Pause/Resume inspection.
* High-contrast color gradient for spotting weak CW and digital signals.
- Flexible Docking: Use inline inside the main workspace or undock to a second monitor.
title: 9. SDR Audio Spectrum & Waterfall

body:
High-speed contesting module compliant with international contest rules:

- Supported Contests: CQ WW DX, CQ WPX, ARRL DX, IARU HF Championship, SP DX Contest, VHF/UHF contests, and custom user-defined rules.
- Smart Exchange Parser: Single-line exchange entry (e.g. '599 001' or '599 15') automatically splits RST, serial number, CQ/ITU zone, or province.
- Live Score & Rate Sheet: Real-time QSO/hour rate (10-min and 60-min), multiplier matrix by band, and total score calculation.
- Export Formats: Generates official Cabrillo 3.0 logs, EDI (VHF/UHF) logs, and ADIF/ADX files.
title: 10. Contest Engine & Cabrillo

body:
Automatic progress tracking across major international and national award programs:

- DXCC: Mixed, Band (160m–6m), Mode (CW, Phone, Digital), and DXCC Challenge matrix with Worked vs. Confirmed status.
- WAZ, WAS & WAE: Tracks all 40 CQ Zones, 50 US States (with built-in States Browser), and European WAE entities.
- Polska Gmina Award (PGA): Complete database of all 2,477 Polish municipalities.
- SOTA, POTA, WWFF & IOTA: Dedicated reference fields, built-in IOTA Island Browser, and compliant SOTA CSV export.
title: 11. Awards & Field Programs

body:
Manage paper QSL confirmations and print address/QSO labels:

- Vector PDF Label Exporter: Generates print-ready A4 PDF sheets for standard Avery templates (3x8, 3x7, 2x8, 2x7 labels per page).
- Smart Print Queue: Filter QSOs waiting for paper QSLs by band, mode, or date range, with automatic multi-page pagination.
- Margin Calibration: Fine-tune horizontal and vertical offsets in millimeters for any laser or inkjet printer.
- Visual QSL Card Designer: Customize background, callsign typography, QSO data table, and station notes.
title: 12. QSL Designer & Avery PDF Labels

body:
Comprehensive data exchange and cloud logbook synchronization:

- ADIF 3.1.5 & ADX: Full import/export compatibility with standard .adi and XML .adx files.
- Online Logbooks: Direct two-way or upload synchronization with ARRL LoTW (via TQSL), eQSL.cc, Club Log, QRZ.com Logbook, HamQTH, Cloudlog, and HRDLog.net.
- Resilient Upload Scheduler: Persistent queue with automatic retry and exponential backoff.
- Online Database Updater: One-click download and live reload of MASTER.SCP (Super Check Partial) and the LoTW user activity list; country files (DXCC prefixes) are installed separately.
- Built-in REST & WebSocket API (port 8080): Local Axum server for third-party integrations.
title: 13. Cloud Sync, ADIF & REST API

body:
Extend SPLogbook safely with sandboxed user scripts:

- Rhai Scripting Sandbox: Write custom .rhai plugins without recompiling the application. Strict operation and memory limits keep the UI responsive.
- Lifecycle Hooks: on_startup(), on_qso_logged(call_sign, band, mode, freq_mhz, is_atno), on_dx_spot(spotter, dx_call, freq_khz, band, comment, is_ft8), on_spot_badge(dx_call, band, freq_khz, badge), on_rig_state(freq_mhz, mode, connected), on_band_opened(band), on_workspace_changed(name), on_pota_info(reference, name, active), on_sota_info(reference, name, points), on_contest_qso(call_sign, band, mode, sent, received, contest), on_wsjtx_decode(call_sign, grid, snr, freq_hz, message, is_cq, mark).
- Read-only functions and plugin memory: worked_before(call), worked_before(call, band, mode), dxcc_of(call), band_of(freq_mhz), bandplan_mode(freq_mhz), language(), utc_date(), utc_time(), utc_hour(), memory_get(key), memory_set(key, value), switch_page(name). Each hook call is limited to 50 ms and 200 log queries, and a plugin keeps at most 64 keys in its memory per session.
- Command Bridge: Scripts can trigger CW macros, voice keyer messages, rotator headings, audio alerts, and QSO fields.
- Built-in Plugin Marketplace: One-click installation of curated plugins (POTA Helper, CW Macros, Contest Assistant, Rotor Assistant, Band Activity Logger).
title: 14. User Plugins (Rhai) & Marketplace

body:
Secure multi-station Host/Peer operation over a local LAN or private VPN tunnel:

- Host/Peer Architecture: One station operates as Host (listening on a chosen TCP port, default 7373), while other stations connect as Peers by specifying the Host IP/hostname and port.
- Authenticated Encryption: All network frames are encrypted with XChaCha20-Poly1305. Session keys are derived via Argon2id from a random salt and shared secret. Passwords are never transmitted in plaintext.
- Replay and Reorder Protection: Every frame includes a monotonic counter and unique identifier, preventing replay and reordering attacks.
- Catch-up Inventory Replication: Upon establishing an authenticated session, stations exchange SHA-256 journal inventories and checksums for the active journal, automatically transferring missing QSOs bidirectionally without duplicates.
- Status Diagnostics & Reconnect: The Multi-Op window displays live connection status (Listening, Connected, Reconnecting, Error). Clear errors indicate bad secrets ('Invalid password or secret') or protocol version mismatches ('Unsupported protocol version'). If network connectivity is lost, Peers automatically attempt reconnection every 5 seconds.
- Synchronization Boundaries & Limitations:
* Sync operates strictly on the active journal.
* Only new QSO additions are synchronized; edits and deletions are not propagated across peers.
* Designed for trusted local networks (LAN) or secure private VPN tunnels. Direct exposure to the public Internet without VPN is not recommended.
* Ensure the firewall permits inbound TCP traffic on the configured port (default 7373).
title: 15. Encrypted Multi-Op Sync (LAN/VPN)

body:
SPLogbook runs natively on 64-bit Windows 10/11 and GNU/Linux. Key platform notes:

GNU/Linux (x86_64):
1. USB Serial Port Permissions:
Add your user account to the serial group to access /dev/ttyUSB* and /dev/ttyACM*:
- Debian / Ubuntu / Mint / Raspberry Pi OS:
sudo usermod -aG dialout $USER
- Arch / Manjaro / Fedora / openSUSE:
sudo usermod -aG uucp $USER
Log out and log back in after running the command.
2. Data Directories (XDG Standard):
- Databases & logs: ~/.local/share/splogbook/
- Configuration: ~/.config/splogbook/

Microsoft Windows (10 / 11 64-bit):
1. Virtual COM Ports: Install the transceiver manufacturer's USB UART driver (Silicon Labs CP210x, FTDI, or CH340) and select the detected COM port in CAT Settings.
2. Windows Firewall: Allow SPLogbook on private networks when using the WSJT-X UDP bridge (2237), CAT proxy (4534), or Multi-Op LAN sync.
3. Data Directory: Stored in %APPDATA%\SPLogbook\
title: 16. Windows & Linux Setup

body:
Answers to common technical questions:

Q: My transceiver does not connect via CAT.
A: 1. Make sure no other program (WSJT-X, OmniRig, N1MM) holds the same COM/tty serial port open.
2. Check that the baud rate in the CAT settings matches the radio menu (often 19200 or 38400, 115200 on newer radios).
3. On Linux, make sure your account belongs to the dialout or uucp group.

Q: ATNO sound alerts are silent or the Voice Keyer does not play files.
A: Check in the system volume mixer that SPLogbook is not muted and that the default audio output device is active. Voice messages must be standard WAV files.

Q: How do I know that “Update online databases (SCP, LoTW)” has finished?
A: The program downloads MASTER.SCP and the LoTW user activity list in the background, loads them at once and reports the result in a notification. Country files are installed separately: Tools → References → Download current country files (Big CTY)… or Import country files from disk…

Q: The DX Cluster disconnects right after connecting.
A: DXSpider and AR-Cluster nodes require a valid callsign at login. Enter your callsign in the station settings; with N0CALL the program logs in with the guest callsign SP0LOG.

Q: How do I restore the log from a backup?
A: Choose Log → Restore Database from Backup…, pick a .db file in the backups folder and confirm. Before replacing anything the program saves a copy of the current database, checks the selected copy and refuses a copy made by a newer version. If any step fails, the current database is put back. After a restore the log, awards and SCP are reloaded.

Q: At start the program reports an unexpected end of the previous session.
A: The previous session did not close normally (crash or power loss). The program checked the database and saved a copy marked unclean_shutdown in the backups folder. Usually nothing more is needed; if the log looks damaged, restore that copy or an earlier one.

Q: Can I move my logbook database to another computer?
A: Yes. Copy default_log.db (or a copy from the backups folder) from the folder opened by Help → Open App Data Directory. On Linux this is ~/.local/share/splogbook/databases. SQLite files are fully compatible between Windows and Linux.
title: 17. Troubleshooting FAQ
